headline: Council welcomes Fukuyama City Assembly members, discusses Lahaina recovery

meeting.summary: At a special meeting, council members spoke on power, West Maui water, federal rebuilding aid and a County insurance gap program. The delegation gave the Council a denim tablecloth and was to leave for a UH Maui College presentation.
meeting.recap: The Maui County Council held a special meeting to welcome members of the Fukuyama City Assembly.[[0:01:59]] The chair said a resolution adopted on February 11, 2008, made Fukuyama City a sister city of Maui County.[[0:02:12]] A guest asked who is in charge of water and power as Lahaina recovers.[[0:17:47]] A council member said the power company shuts off power when wind is over 45 miles per hour and humidity is under 45 percent.[[0:19:47]] A council member said the County controls delivery of 23 percent of West Maui water, and private companies deliver 77 percent.[[0:21:33]] The member said the Council recently approved buying three water systems.[[0:22:03]] The member said reclaimed water use fell from 5 million to about 3 million gallons a day after the fire.[[0:23:05]] A council member said federal paperwork makes it hard for families to get rebuilding money.[[0:25:59]] A speaker said the federal government gave 1.6 billion dollars for housing and rebuilding.[[0:27:34]] A council member said the County started an insurance gap program to help homeowners rebuild.[[0:34:41]] The member said the gap is often $300,000 to $500,000.[[0:35:07]] The delegation gave the Council a denim tablecloth as a gift.[[0:47:13]]
meeting.next: The chair said the delegation would leave for an evening presentation at UH Maui College after a group photo.
